call.test: uv run --no-cache --isolated --no-project --with ./organize-downloads python3 -m unittest discover -s organize-downloads/tests -t organize-downloads

receiver: whoever runs the tool and whoever maintains it, a person or an AI
use: running organize-downloads with nothing added, or with a folder given last, to see where each file would go with nothing changed, and maintaining it with the tests of T3.2 passing

questions.question: Building the package with setuptools from organize-downloads (as pipx install ./organize-downloads and the uv test command do) writes organize-downloads/src/organize_downloads.egg-info (and may write build/), but this CCS lets the run write only the seven code and workflow paths, not organize-downloads/.gitignore; if that ignore file does not already keep these out, the run cannot keep files a run makes out of the repository (B-5). May the run also write organize-downloads/.gitignore, adding it to the CCS paths?
questions.recommended: Yes, add organize-downloads/.gitignore to the CCS paths, so the files the build makes are ignored in the same change that first makes them, as T3.2 did for __pycache__/.

answers.answer: Answer to your B-5 question: no change to the CCS is needed. organize-downloads/.gitignore, made in T3.2 and already in the repository, holds __pycache__/, build/ and *.egg-info/, each with a comment, so what the build makes is already kept out. Go on with the run.

questions.question: Three behaviors of the code are held by no test of T3.2: the stop on a folder that cannot be read (cli.py lines 37-38, the only lines coverage finds unrun), the escaping of file names that cannot be printed as they are (bytes not valid UTF-8, a line break), and which condition a folder stop names ('does not exist' or 'is not a folder'). This run may write only the seven code and workflow paths, so it cannot add those tests. May the run also write organize-downloads/tests/test_cli.py and organize-downloads/tests/test_folder.py, adding them to the CCS paths?
questions.recommended: Yes, add test_cli.py and test_folder.py to the CCS paths, so each of these behaviors gets a test in the same change that brings it, and a fault in it fails a test, as B-6 asks.

answers.answer: Answer to your B-6 question: yes; the CCS now holds organize-downloads/tests/test_cli.py and organize-downloads/tests/test_folder.py as further paths of the work, with a "chosen" entry saying why. Read the CCS anew and go on with the run.

back.did: Read each module for knowledge written twice. Ran `git status --porcelain --ignored organize-downloads` after the test runs: build/, *.egg-info, and both __pycache__ folders show as ignored ('!!'), so that part holds. Looked for where the command's name is written.
back.lacking: The command's name is held in cli.PROGRAM (cli.py:18, used as argparse's prog and before every stop) and again as a literal in folder._GIVE_A_FOLDER, 'give the folder to organize last: organize-downloads <folder>' (folder.py:14). Changing PROGRAM leaves every Folder finder stop telling the user to type the old command. The name is written in two places in the code itself, apart from the console-script name in pyproject.toml, which must be there. The rest held: the type table is in type_table.py alone, the stop action in one constant, and the files a run makes are ignored.

back.did: Ran coverage.py with --branch over the whole test run: 100% of statements and branches. Copied the project to a mktemp folder and ran mutmut there through uv, leaving out test_stories.py: its source-versus-installed check fails on every mutant because mutmut's copy differs from the installed one, and nothing in the repository says so. Of 273 mutants, 204 were killed and 69 survived. Read each surviving diff with `mutmut show`. Some survivors change no behavior (follow_symlinks=None, codec names in other letter case, last_extension giving 'XXXX' in place of '' for a name with no dot), so I set those aside.
back.lacking: Mutants that change behavior survive with nothing written that says the gap was decided. (1) cli.py:32 with platform.system() replaced by None (mutmut x_main__mutmut_5) survives. The cli test with no folder given makes a home that names Downloads both the macOS and the Linux way, so no test fails when main stops passing the real system's name. On macOS with no user-dirs file, the run would then stop instead of listing ~/Downloads, which breaks AC6. (2) folder.py:78 with "$HOME" mutated (x__download_folder_named_in__mutmut_19/20) survives. Settings naming $HOME then give the 'names no download folder' stop instead of the 'names your home folder itself' stop, and test_folder.py:219-229 asserts only that the settings path is in the message, not which condition is named. The given-path stops' prefixes ('the Downloads folder ', 'the download folder <settings> names, ', mutants 13, 20-22, 36 of find_organized_folder) are not held either. (3) The output around the listing is held by no test. 'No file to move in <folder>.' replaced by None (x__print_moves__mutmut_2/4) survives, because test_cli.py:89-97 checks only that no move line is printed. The trailing 'Nothing was moved.' line (mutmut 22-25) and the plural 'N files' heading (mutmut_7, always 'file') survive too. (4) --help is built on every run but its text is never checked: 33 mutants in _parser and _help_epilog survive. These include the column width +2 changed to -2 or +3, the wrap width dropped, and the folder argument's help removed, so the help no longer showing every AC3 extension under its folder, or the left-in-place rules, would fail no test.

chosen.chosen: The unreadable-folder test makes a real folder with mode 000 and is skipped when run as root.
chosen.why: It checks the true path from os.scandir through the planner to the stop; root reads any folder, so there the case cannot be made, and GitHub Actions runs as a user that is not root.

chosen.chosen: The invalid-byte test hands the planner's result (a name decoded from b"bad\xff.pdf") in place of the planner instead of making such a file.
chosen.why: macOS's file system refuses to make a file whose name is not valid UTF-8, and AC7 asks the tests to hold on both systems.

chosen.chosen: A broken symbolic link given as the folder counts as 'is not a folder', and a link to a folder is organized; both held by tests.
chosen.why: This is what the code already does (os.path.lexists), and the link itself is there; testing both keeps the decision's rules from changing unnoticed.

questions.question: Mutation testing with mutmut (run through uv on a copy, test_stories.py left out) now kills 270 of 272 mutants; statement and branch coverage is 100%. The two left change no behavior: organize.py line 37 `entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)` made `follow_symlinks=None` (None counts as false just the same), and type_table.py line 39 `""` for a name with no dot made `"XXXX"` (both go to Others and neither is a downloading ending, as no extension in the table is "xxxx"). No test can fail on either, and B-6 asks that a mutant left out has beside it what the user decided and why. May the run leave these two, with a one-line comment beside each line saying no behavior changes with that mutant and why?
questions.recommended: Yes, a one-line comment beside each of the two lines, since no test can tell these mutants apart from the code and the comment keeps the next maintainer from taking them for a gap.
